skill.name: budget-pacing-monitor
skill.description: Monitors live advertising spend against a target curve, identifies pacing issues, checks learning status, and recommends when budget reallocation needs review.
skill.summary: Evaluate campaign spend pacing and identify reallocation triggers.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, documentation links, homepage URLs, and ordinary campaign-monitoring language. Two findings are confirmed: the command template uses an unquoted campaign value, and the save template does not require filename sanitization.

remediation.issue: The ledger command places the campaign value into a shell command without quoting or validation.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the campaign as a safely escaped argument, reject shell metacharacters, and use an argument separator supported by the script.

remediation.issue: The save filename includes a user-controlled campaign value without normalization.
remediation.suggestion: Convert campaign names to an allowlisted slug and verify the resolved path remains inside memory/ad/budget-pacing-monitor.

content.value_statement: Campaign spend can drift from plan before teams recognize the problem. This skill compares current spend with a target curve and identifies review triggers.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative campaign spend with even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curves.
Classifies pacing as on-track, ahead, behind, or stalled.
Calculates percent-to-pace from actual and expected cumulative spend.
Checks learning-phase status before recommending a reallocation review.
Distinguishes observed pacing gaps from plausible delivery causes.
Projects end-of-flight spend for lifetime budgets using the current rate.
limitations: Requires a campaign budget, flight window, target curve, and daily spend data.
Does not calculate a new budget allocation or select a bidding strategy.
Cannot verify pacing reliably from one dashboard screenshot or one cumulative total.
Referenced ledger scripts and repository documents may be unavailable in a standalone installation.

use_cases.title: Review Weekly Campaign Delivery
use_cases.description: Compare current spend with the planned curve and identify campaigns outside the accepted pacing band.

use_cases.title: Investigate Spend Spikes
use_cases.description: Separate an observed pacing increase from possible causes such as cap exhaustion, audience limits, or dayparting.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reallocation Decisions
use_cases.description: Document pacing evidence, learning status, forecast spend, and a clear trigger before reviewing budget changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Pacing
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for [campaign]. Budget is [amount], flight dates are [dates], and cumulative spend is [amount]. Use an even target curve.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first pacing check with basic campaign data

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Daily Spend
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this daily spend export for [campaign]. Compare it with a [curve] target and classify delivery as on-track, ahead, behind, or stalled.
prompt_templates.scenario: A campaign has daily spend history and a defined target curve

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Pace Gap
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this pacing gap using spend, serving status, learning status, and budget-loss metrics. Separate measured evidence from plausible causes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs the likely driver of over-delivery or under-delivery

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Reallocation Trigger
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [campaign portfolio] against a [percentage] pacing band. Forecast final spend, apply learning safeguards, and identify campaigns needing reallocation review.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced portfolio review with explicit decision thresholds

output_examples.input: Campaign X spent $1,800 after 9 days of a 30-day flight with a $6,000 lifetime budget.
output_examples.output: Expected spend is $1,800 on an even curve. The campaign is at 100% of pace and is On-track. Hold reallocation.

output_examples.input: Campaign Y spent 30% of its budget after 60% of the flight. Learning has ended.
output_examples.output: Campaign Y is at 50% of pace and is Behind. Review bid throttling, audience limits, and serving status before reallocating funds.

output_examples.input: Campaign Z is at 138% of pace but remains in the platform learning phase.
output_examples.output: Campaign Z is Ahead, but the pacing read is observational. Hold changes until learning ends, then check the stated pacing band again.

best_practices: Set the target curve and pacing band before reviewing current spend.
Use daily exports and confirm learning status before acting on a pacing gap.
Label every value as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
anti_patterns: Do not infer daily pacing from one cumulative spend total or a screenshot.
Do not change the target curve after seeing results to make delivery appear on-track.
Do not trigger budget changes while the campaign remains in learning.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide the budget, flight dates, target curve, daily spend, learning status, and available delivery metrics.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to advertising platforms?
faq.answer: No direct connection is required. It primarily analyzes manually exported account data, while optional connectors depend on the host environment.

faq.question: What does percent-to-pace mean?
faq.answer: It divides actual cumulative spend by expected cumulative spend at the same point in the planned curve.

faq.question: Can it recommend a new budget amount?
faq.answer: No. It identifies whether a reallocation review is warranted, but another planning process must calculate the new allocation.

faq.question: How does learning status affect the result?
faq.answer: The skill reports pacing during learning as observational and holds reallocation triggers until learning ends.

faq.question: Can results be saved?
faq.answer: Yes, after user approval. Campaign names should be sanitized before they become filenames.
